text:
alex: Quick async — need eyes on API contract for model selection / routing. Codeowners: @maya @sam. Two quick Qs and a small proposal. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/1234. 1) Priority rules when client sends model_ids (array), region_hint and tier_hint — what should win? 2) Response shape: we currently expose served_model and fallback_chain; clients (SDKs) depend on a flat string for served_model and list-of-strings for fallback_chain. I changed runtime to return richer objects; need a backwards-compatible contract. PTAL when you have cycles.

maya: Looking. Current informal rule in routing is: explicit pin (single model_id exact match) > model_hint list order > region/tier routing policy. If client sets model_id (not list) we treat as pin. We should document and enforce. :+1:

sam: Re: priority — for latency-sensitive customers I think region_hint should beat model_hint order (i.e., prefer local variant even if later in hint list). Can we make the policy configurable per-tenant?

alex: Good point. Proposal: default policy = pin > model_hint_order > region/tier. Add per-tenant override to switch to pin > region_priority > model_hint_order. Will add flag in TenantRoutingConfig.

jin: Quick question about the response shape — what exactly is runtime returning now? Example from staging: \n```json\n{\n  \"served_model\": {\"id\":\"m-latest-quant\",\"variant\":\"q4_0\"},\n  \"fallback_chain\": [{\"id\":\"m-old\",\"reason\":\"capacity\"}],\n  \"region\":\"us-west-2\"\n}\n```\nClients expect: served_model: \"m-latest-quant\" and fallback_chain: [\"m-old\"]. Do we need to keep that flat format?

alex: We must keep flat format for backward compat. My proposal: always include legacy fields and add extended ones. E.g. add served_model_id (string) and fallback_chain_ids (array of strings) alongside richer served_model_detail / fallback_chain_details. SDKs can migrate when ready.

maya: I like that. Concrete contract: \n- served_model: string (legacy)\n- served_model_detail: object (optional) with fields {id, variant, quantization, node_id}\n- fallback_chain: [string] (legacy)\n- fallback_details: [object] (optional)\nAlso add served_original_request: {requested_models: [string]} so we keep client intent traceable.

sam: Also need to call out behavior for auto-fallback to quantized variant: do we set served_model to quantized id or the requested id? SDKs check served_model to decide feature flags.

esther: SDK owner ping — I'll need to map fields. Prefer served_model always reflect the actual model used (variant id). If we add original_requested/intent we can preserve mapping. I'll open SDK PR once contract lands.

alex: Agreed — served_model should be the actual model id (variant). Add served_requested_ids: [string] to response.

jin: One more: fallback_chain format — prefer to keep fallback_chain as strings for now and add fallback_metadata optional array, not fallback_details because naming collision with other services. Example: \n```json\n\"fallback_chain\": [\"m-a\",\"m-b\"],\n\"fallback_metadata\": [{\"id\":\"m-a\",\"reason\":\"overloaded\"}]\n```\n
maya: Sounds good. We should also add a deprecation note: keep legacy fields for at least 3 months and emit a warning header X-Runtime-Contract-Warning when we include legacy aliases.

routing-bot: staging rollout for routing-service v2 at 2024-11-08T10:30:00Z. Will run compatibility tests defined in /infra/tests/routing_contract_compat.

sam: FYI I'll open a short RFC for per-tenant routing priority toggles and attach a migration plan for SDKs.

esther: On SDK PR: question — if we always return served_model (variant id), will telemetry and billing still map properly to customer's requested model? Need a mapping table in usage pipeline. I'll coordinate with billing.

alex: Noted. I'll add mapping hook to telemetry pipeline (add original_requested_ids).

alex: Thanks everyone — I updated PR 1234 to include: legacy aliases, served_requested_ids, fallback_metadata and the warning header. I'll merge after @maya and @esther approve; if no objections by EOD I'll merge. :pray:
